text:
lin: Heads-up: rolling perf anomaly after yesterday's kernel-routing tweak. Small-chat workload shows host-side work increase. Placing raw notes here.

lin: baseline small-chat p50/p95 host-parse: 110ms / 200ms
lin: post-change p50/p95 host-parse: 130ms / 340ms :confused: 

lin: quick sample top-delta:
```
parse_tokenize   +24%
memcpy           +13%
grpc_readv       +6%
kv_lookup        -2%
```

jas: memcpy and grpc_readv up — sounds like we're linearizing fragments on each ingress and doing extra syscalls per tiny write. Which change did this come from?

lin: The new routing picks "segvec_fast" kernel pre-batching when seq_len <= 56. To satisfy the kernel we flatten iov fragments into a contiguous buffer with a memcpy + per-request alloc. That happens before the batcher merges requests.

nik: So for batches of N small requests we're doing N memcpys and N allocs, and then batcher merges into another buffer -> double work. Yikes.

bench-bot: CI smoke (canary vs baseline): throughput -3.5%, host-parse CPU +18%, small-chat p95 +70%, allocs/sec +40%.

margo: Short fix idea: 1) revert pre-batch selector change 2) implement sticky linearize buffer pool (per-worker reuse) 3) or postpone kernel selection to post-merge (decide on packed batch region). All three should be fast to try.

jas: I prefer postponing selection until after batching because if we pick kernel post-merge we only linearize once per batch for contiguous kernels. That amortizes cost. Sticky pool is lower risk though.

lin: Agreed. Sticky pool is lowest-risk short-term. Post-batch selection is the right end-state but touches batcher codepath.

nik: Also watch KV cache semantics: if we change the canonical bytes used for the kvcache key (prelinearized vs original fragments) we might perturb hit-rate. Add a kvcache_key_source tag.

margo: I'll add telemetry fields: kernel_choice, linearize_mode=[none,sticky,prebatch,postbatch], sticky_hit_rate, preparse_copies, batch_merged=true/false, kvcache_key_source.

jas: Microbench plan: replay small-chat trace at 2k QPS with variations: A) baseline, B) prebatch-linearize (current), C) sticky-pool, D) postbatch-select + single linearize. Measure p50/p95, allocs/sec, memcpy ms breakdown, kvcache hit-rate.

lin: I'll spin up sticky-pool PR behind feature flag: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/2401 (sticky-pool w/ per-thread ring buffer). Patch will avoid heap allocs on pool hit and mark metric sticky_reuse_ratio.

nik: For postbatch-select, ensure batch metadata records per-request fragment layout so kernel can pick segmented kernel when necessary. That avoids copies entirely if kernel can process iovecs. Might be longer-term: RTX-5050 (kernel-iovec support).

bench-bot: Sticky-pool PR CI perf quickcheck: host-parse CPU -4% vs bad canary, allocs/sec -85% vs bad canary. Full replay pending.

margo: If sticky-pool lifts the tail, we can keep postbatch-select for later. But still submit design for kernel iovec acceptance.

jas: One more thing: grpc path shows readv/writev syscalls rising. We should add an ingress coalescer that groups small writes into a local buffer and issues fewer syscalls. Prototype a coalescer in ingress layer and measure syscall counts.

lin: Good call — I'll prototype a small coalescing buffer for gRPC chunk writes. If it reduces syscall pressure it'll help p95 on busy hosts.

nik: Also add a quick KV-diff run: replay with sticky-pool on and compare kvcache hit-rate per-key to baseline to ensure keys are identical. If not, we need a normalization step.

lin: TL;DR plan: 1) revert prebatch selector on canary (done) 2) land sticky-pool behind flag + run microbench 3) prototype postbatch-selector and ingress coalescer 4) long-term: kernel-iovec design (RTX-5050).

margo: Filing follow-ups: RTX-5022 sticky-pool implementation, RTX-5023 ingress-coalescer prototype, RTX-5024 postbatch-selector experiment, RTX-5050 kernel-iovec design.

lin: Post-rollback quick numbers: host-parse p95 back to 208ms, memcpy portion down to 2% in perf sample. Revert confirmed effective.

jas: Thanks all — great fast detection + rollback. Please paste microbench results here once done and tag perf dash.

lin: Will do. Attaching small repro script and a flame screenshot to RTX-5022.
